title: Rapid mitigation guide: API key compromise + rate blast
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact on-call-friendly mitigation and post-incident review guide for scenarios where a leaked API key (or set of keys) is used by a third-party aggregator/proxy to generate sudden token-heavy request bursts ("rate blast"). It mixes immediate triage commands, short-term mitigations, and a lightweight postmortem checklist.

Intended audience:
on-call SREs, platform on-call, solutions-eng responding to customer escalations, security responders.

Summary (one-liner):
Leaked service keys allowed an external aggregator to pump requests through the hosted API, causing quota exhaustion and elevated tail latency for several customers; partial WAF rules and rapid per-key throttles mitigated impact.

When to use this guide:
- Alerts: sudden spike in requests-per-key > 50x baseline and token consumption spike flagged by billing/usage pipeline
- Customers reporting degraded throughput while overall cluster utilization is sub-70% (indicates skewed traffic)
- Suspicious agent strings or repeated user-agent patterns (third-party aggregator signatures)

Detection signals to check first (fast):
- dashboard: /app/console/requests-per-key (last 15m) — sort desc
- billing spikes: daily_tokens_by_key metric (in last 1h)
- WAF logs: repeated blocked/native 403s from same src ip / user-agent
- Auth logs: many failed key-verify attempts followed by success from same IP range
- Netflow: repeated identical-sized requests (indicates automated client)

Quick triage timeline (start stopwatch):
- 00–03m: identify top 10 keys by token consumption (query infra metrics)
- 03–06m: check if keys belong to a single customer or are cross-customer
- 05–10m: add short-term throttle or block for keys/IPs; notify product security and CS for affected customers
- 10–30m: deploy WAF rule to fingerprint aggregator user-agent / client IP set; monitor for collateral block
- 30–90m: issue key rotation for compromised keys (see rotation steps) or create emergency per-customer quota increases if legitimate workloads are impacted and keys are not compromised

Immediate mitigation steps (operational playbook):
1) Identify affected keys
   - run: SELECT key_id, sum(tokens) FROM usage_metrics WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY key_id ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 50;
   - If DB access slow, use pre-aggregated graphite/cortex metric: metrics.requests.tokens.by_key.top(50, "30m").

2) Place fast per-key throttle (preferred)
   - Use admin API: POST /admin/keys/{key_id}/throttle {"rate": "50r/m"}
   - If admin API not reachable, set in redis gate: HSET key_throttle {key_id} 50

3) Block suspicious source IP ranges (short-term)
   - Add CIDR to emergency blocklist: ./scripts/emergency-waf-add 203.0.113.0/24 --reason "rate-blast"
   - Verify WAF counters in 5m to ensure false positive rate < 1% of baseline requests

4) Create temporary routing fallback for premium customers
   - Route small percentage (5–10%) to dedicated capacity pool with reserved tokens to preserve SLAs

5) Issue emergency key rotation for confirmed compromised keys
   - Steps: disable key -> create rotated key -> update customer's integration guidance -> send rotation email
   - Automation: /ops/key-rotation --key {key_id} --rotate-now --notify-cs
   - If keys are embedded in partner's SDK, ask partner to push new release or provide manual rotation token via secure channel

6) If attack appears distributed (many keys), apply global rate-limiter tuning and emergency quota policy
   - Increase global per-IP request smoothing window from 1s to 5s
   - Apply token bucket adjustments: tokens_per_minute = max( tokens_per_minute, baseline*2 ) for internal bulk services only

Forensics checklist (collect evidence early):
- Export WAF logs covering first 2 hours of spike into S3: /ops/export-waf-logs --start ... --end ...
- Take snapshots of auth service logs and index to ELK for search
- Record top 50 user-agents and client IPs in incident ticket
- Preserve raw request samples (first 1000 requests) for security team review (PII redaction required)

Communication templates (quick fragments for Slack/email):
- Customer notification (CS): "We observed anomalous token consumption on key XXXXX leading to intermittent errors. We've temporarily throttled the key and are rotating credentials. We will follow up with a new key and mitigation timeline."
- Internal alert (#sre): "Rate-blast detected: top key k_12345 causing 72% of token consumption. Throttle applied; WAF rule pushed. Looking for root cause. Triage lead: @maya. Ticket SRE-7812."

Post-incident runbook review items (owner + target dates):
- Verify key rotation automation covers partner-embedded keys (owner: Carlos Mendes, due: 2026-03-01)
- Add detection rule: "abnormal tokens-per-key zscore > 6 for 15m" (owner: Liam Patel, due: 2026-02-20)
- Harden admin API auth for emergency throttle endpoints (owner: eng-api, due: 2026-04-01)
- Add opt-in per-customer emergency quota reserve for top-50 customers (owner: product, due: 2026-03-15)

Metrics to review in retrospective:
- total tokens/min during event vs baseline
- 95th and 99th latency percentiles for affected endpoints
- percentage of requests blocked by WAF vs throttled
- number of affected customers and mean time to restore key (MTR)

Acceptance criteria for adding to permanent runbook:
- Automated detection alerts fire in under 15m with clear top-5 keys listed
- Admin throttle API can be applied within 3 minutes with audit logging
- WAF rule rollout includes automated rate-limit rollback if false positive rate > 2% after 15m observation window

Playbook new items / TODOs:
- Add playbook step for interacting with cloud marketplaces where keys are issued by resellers (edge case seen in 2025-Q4)
- Add canned SQL/metrics queries to central runbook page (Confluence) so on-call doesn't hunt
- Create a small service to precompute tokens-by-key top-100 every 1m and expose read-only endpoint for on-call

Unresolved questions we should track:
- Should we auto-rotate keys that exceed 10x daily average for 3 consecutive days, or wait for manual review? (tradeoff: disruption vs safety)
- What is the acceptable false positive threshold for WAF blocks when responding to a rate blast that resembles legitimate bot traffic?

Appendix: useful commands and locations
- metrics CLI: infra-metrics query --metric tokens_by_key --window 30m --top 50
- emergency throttle: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://admin.api.internal/keys/k_12345/throttle -d '{"rate":"50r/m"}'
- export WAF logs: /ops/export-waf-logs --from=2026-02-11T12:00 --to=2026-02-11T14:00 --out s3://redwood-incidents/sre-7812
- sample sql: SELECT key_id, client_ip, user_agent, count(*) as reqs, sum(tokens) as tokens FROM request_log WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY key_id, client_ip, user_agent ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 200;

Notes to self (on-call rough):
- prioritize per-key throttle over global cluster-wide restriction to minimize collateral damage
- rotate keys proactively when proof of compromise is strong (IP sinks, credentials in public pastebins)
- coordinate public-facing comms with legal and CS if customer data or privacy may be involved

Change log:
- 2025-11-04: initial draft (Maya Chen)
- 2026-01-10: added emergency throttle CLI and WAF rollback criteria (Liam Patel)
- 2026-02-12: added post-incident tickets and metric z-score detection suggestion (Sofia Rossi)

End of guide.
